title: Gigantic Triceps Exercises: My 3 favorite long-head builders
summary: NH demonstrates his three favourite exercises for the long head of the triceps, which he considers the most undertrained part of the arm: the seated dumbbell French press, a skull crusher done with the shoulders fully flexed, and a supinated band or cable extension with shoulder flexion for pump and active recovery. He says a big long head also makes the biceps look bigger.
claims: The long head is the meatiest part of the triceps but is undertrained because it sits under the arm and is not a beach muscle; it creates the fullness under the flexed biceps
Lifters who do a lot of pressing build the lateral head and neglect the long head
For the dumbbell French press pick a weight you can do for at least 6 reps; going to failure is fairly safe because you can drop the dumbbell, but a manageable load protects the elbows
French press setup: cup the inner plates with both hands instead of gripping the handle, rest the dumbbell on the upper chest, press it up and to the side, then lower it behind the head
Sit with only part of your glutes on the bench, upper arms clear of it, torso upright or slightly leaning back, and brace with a big rib cage before each rep
On the French press, do not lock out at the top; focus on the deep stretch at the bottom, not the top of the movement
To finish a heavy French press set, drop the dumbbell if your gym allows it; catching a heavy dumbbell as it falls can hurt your lower back
The French press is easy on the elbows for most people; adjust torso angle or hand position to fit your build
The skull crusher was meant as a long-head isolation exercise, but powerlifting coaches turned it into a compound press

His skull crusher: set up arched like a bench press with any grip width (he prefers wide), let the upper arms travel back into full shoulder flexion, then move only the elbows; the shoulders stay still, so it is not a pullover
The conventional skull crusher with upper arms vertical is still fine; his version is for maximising long-head stretch
Isolation work for the long head should still be hard, but light high-rep pump work also has a place
Use a supinated band or cable triceps extension with shoulder flexion as pump work, active recovery or nucleus overload, especially when the elbows are too cranky for heavy long-head work
Extending the elbow while bringing the shoulder into the movement shifts work to the long head; straight elbow extension mostly works the lateral head
On the band extension, skip the lockout because most of the tension is in the middle of the range
For years NH trained only his biceps, so his triceps lagged; he is now catching up
A developed triceps long head props up the biceps and makes it, including its side peak, look bigger
exercises: cup the plates, rest on upper chest, press up and to the side behind the head, part of the glutes on the bench, upright torso, big brace, no lockout, deep stretch, drop the dumbbell at the end
maximal long-head stretch and easy on the elbows
arch like a bench press, any grip, let the upper arms go back to full shoulder flexion, then only the elbows move
biases the long head; shoulders stay still so it is not a pullover
Supinated band/cable triceps extension with shoulder flexion
anchor overhead, supinated grip, elbows close, bring the shoulder with the extension, no lockout
pump, active recovery or nucleus overload for the long head when the elbows are cranky
training_log: says he works with upwards of 60 lb and drops it at the end
